expected.text: Reference (FY2026 10-K Item 1A), three BILL-specific risks: (1) Charge-card credit risk: BILL buys participation interests in the receivables from BILL Divvy Card spend from its Issuing Banks and bears the full credit risk if spending businesses fail to pay (invoice financing adds similar credit risk), so underwriting-model failures or SMB stress can drive charge-offs. (2) Customer-funds / float risk: BILL moves large sums of customer funds daily and earns interest on funds held for customers ($148.4M, ~9% of FY2026 revenue), exposing it to losses from fraud, errors or credit/market events on those funds and to revenue declines as interest rates fall. (3) Interchange dependence: a substantial portion of revenue is interchange fees on BILL Divvy Card and virtual card transactions, whose rates are set by card networks (Visa/Mastercard) and could be cut by network or regulatory changes. Other acceptable company-specific choices: fraud/risk-management failures on payments, dependence on Issuing Banks (Cross River, WEX Bank, WebBank) and card-receivable funding facilities, reliance on accounting-firm/financial-institution/software partners (e.g., Intuit), SMB concentration, payments/money-transmitter regulation.

source.quote: Our BILL Divvy Card offering exposes us to credit risk and other risks related to spending businesses' ability to pay the balances incurred on their BILL Divvy Cards.

expected.text: Reference summary (FY2025 10-K): (1) Product efficacy/defect risk - if Rapid7's security products and services fail to detect vulnerabilities or threats, generate false positives (e.g., from Metasploit's community-contributed exploits), or contain defects, its brand and reputation as a security vendor, customer renewals and liability exposure would suffer. (2) Being a cybersecurity vendor makes Rapid7 itself a prominent target: a breach of its own or its third-party providers' systems or customer data (heightened by Metasploit's profile among hackers) could harm reputation, reduce demand and create significant liabilities. (3) Renewal/expansion dependence - growth depends on customers renewing term subscriptions on equal or better terms and buying more (cross-sell/upsell), with no renewal obligation (notable given ARR was flat in FY2025). Other defensible company-specific choices: the $900M of convertible notes (including $600M due March 2027) and ability to repay; the shift to a consolidated Command Platform/AI offering; activist stockholder JANA (~10.1% owner with a board seat).
